title: DVT and PE: acute, chronic or history
question: Assign the ICD-10-CM code for the patient's deep vein thrombosis or pulmonary embolism (only that code).
note:
Chief Complaint: Follow-up for DVT.

HPI: 90-year-old male presents for follow-up regarding acute deep vein thrombosis of the right femoral vein diagnosed via ultrasound 3 weeks ago. Pt reports adherence to prescribed anticoagulant regimen. Denies calf pain, redness, or warmth. No shortness of breath or chest pain reported. Pt reports stable mobility but notes mild discomfort in the right thigh. No adverse effects from medication noted.

Medication List:
- Rivaroxaban 15 mg daily
- Lisinopril 10 mg daily
- Atorvastatin 20 mg daily

Review of Systems:
Constitutional: No fever, chills, or fatigue.
Respiratory: No SOB, cough, or wheezing.
Cardiovascular: No chest pain or palpitations.
MSK: Mild right thigh discomfort.
Skin: No rashes or lesions.
All other systems reviewed and negative.

Social History: Lives with spouse. Retired. Non-smoker. Occasional alcohol use.

Family History: Father had hypertension. Mother had stroke.

Vitals:
BP: 132/78
HR: 72 (RRR)
Temp: 98.4 F
SpO2: 96% on RA
Weight: 175 lbs

Recent Labs:
WBC: 7.4
Hgb: 13.2
Hct: 40%
Plt: 210
INR: 1.2
Creatinine: 1.1
eGFR: 72

Exam:
General: Alert, oriented x3, in no acute distress.
Respiratory: CTAB, lungs clear to auscultation.
Cardiovascular: RRR, no murmurs.
Extremities: Right lower extremity shows mild edema compared to left. No erythema or warmth noted. Right femoral vein area unremarkable on palpation. Pulses 2+ bilaterally.

Assessment:
1. Acute DVT of the right femoral vein. Pt is in the first months of anticoagulant treatment. Stable.

Plan:
1. Continue Rivaroxaban as prescribed.
2. Monitor for signs of bleeding or worsening symptoms.
3. Follow up in 4 weeks for repeat evaluation.

Electronically signed, L. Moreau, DO, 05/14/2026
explanations: Acute DVT of the right femoral vein, still under initial treatment: I82.411 (HCC 267).

distractors.why: The clot is acute and still being treated.
The DVT is documented as acute.
